papers.title: Operationalizing Document AI: A Microservice Architecture for OCR and LLM Pipelines in Production
papers.innovation: Presents a concrete microservice architecture for production-scale Document AI pipelines, addressing the gap between academic model definition and practical, scalable deployment of multi-model pipelines (e.g., OCR, classification, LLM-based understanding).
papers.benchmarks: Focuses on bridging the gap for running models at production scale, implying architectural robustness, scalability, and reliability for real-world deployment rather than specific model performance metrics. It's about operational efficiency and integration.
papers.use_case: Designing, building, and deploying robust, scalable, and modular Document AI solutions in a production environment, effectively integrating various AI models like OCR and LLMs into a cohesive system.

papers.title: Learn-by-Wire Training Control Governance: Bounded Autonomous Training Under Stress for Stability and Efficiency
papers.innovation: Introduces Learn-by-Wire Guard (LBW-Guard), a novel bounded autonomous training-control governance layer designed to mitigate instability, degraded runs, and wasted compute during large language model training, especially under aggressive learning rates and scale.
papers.benchmarks: Aims to improve training stability and efficiency, reducing wasted compute and preventing degraded runs under challenging conditions. The innovation's success is benchmarked by more reliable and resource-efficient LLM training outcomes.
papers.use_case: Enhancing the reliability and efficiency of large-scale LLM training processes, preventing costly training failures and optimizing resource utilization in high-stress or aggressive training configurations.

papers.title: Embedding by Elicitation: Dynamic Representations for Bayesian Optimization of System Prompts
papers.innovation: Proposes a new method for Bayesian optimization of system prompts that uses 'embedding by elicitation' to create dynamic representations. This allows for effective prompt tuning even when feedback is only available as aggregate metrics, a common and challenging scenario in real-world LLM deployment.
papers.benchmarks: Addresses the difficult problem of prompt optimization where only aggregate metrics (not per-example labels or critiques) are available. The innovation's performance is benchmarked by its ability to effectively tune prompts and improve system behavior under these constrained feedback conditions.
papers.use_case: Automating and optimizing the tuning of system prompts for LLMs and other AI systems, particularly valuable for AI engineers working with limited or aggregate feedback to improve model behavior and performance.
